messages.content: Predict a human responder's decision in a three-person ultimatum game. A proposer divides 15 monetary units (MUs) among the proposer, you (the responder), and a passive other player. You choose accept or reject. Accept gives each player exactly the currently proposed amount; reject gives all three players zero. You cannot revise the allocation. Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. There are two runs of 40 planned trials each. An allocation is displayed for 4 seconds, then a 1-7 second fixation, then a 3-second response period; outcome feedback follows the response, then another 1-7 second fixation. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.

You choose accept or reject. Accept gives each player exactly the currently proposed amount; reject gives all three players zero. You cannot revise the allocation. Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. There are two runs of 40 planned trials each. An allocation is displayed for 4 seconds, then a 1-7 second fixation, then a 3-second response period; outcome feedback follows the response, then another 1-7 second fixation. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.

Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. An allocation is displayed for 4 seconds, then a 1-7 second fixation, then a 3-second response period; outcome feedback follows the response, then another 1-7 second fixation. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.

Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.

You choose accept or reject. Accept gives each player exactly the currently proposed amount; reject gives all three players zero. You cannot revise the allocation. Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. There are two runs of 40 planned trials each. An allocation is displayed for 4 seconds, then a 1-7 second fixation, then a 3-second response period; outcome feedback follows the response, then another 1-7 second fixation. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.

An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. You choose accept or reject. Accept gives each player exactly the currently proposed amount; reject gives all three players zero. You cannot revise the allocation. Participants were told the offers came from proposers and that payment depended on their decisions. The record does not specify the MU-to-currency conversion or exact final payment-selection rule; do not assume one. Written instructions and a comprehension quiz preceded scanning. There are two runs of 40 planned trials each. An allocation is displayed for 4 seconds, then a 1-7 second fixation, then a 3-second response period; outcome feedback follows the response, then another 1-7 second fixation. Buttons are counterbalanced; the required answer is the decision meaning, not a physical button. Each prior recorded entry lists the allocation (proposer, self, other), the responder's earlier decision and its resulting payoffs, already available before the current decision. An unavailable earlier slot means the research export lacks that record, not that the participant saw no allocation or feedback. Do not fill missing history. No individually verified demographic attributes or practice choices are provided. Return exactly accept or reject.
